te: Overseas visit postponed, a model of home farming for older persons in Nakhon Phanom, and medical food for children
se: Following a resolution of the Senate Affairs Committee, the committee agreed to cancel or postpone the bilateral meetings abroad for now. It considered the first round of contest videos (e-cigarettes 72 teams, the power of older persons 16 teams, inequality 27 teams). It received a request to support a model project improving the quality of life of older persons with “smart household farming innovation” in That Phanom District, Nakhon Phanom, and passed it to the subcommittee on older persons. It also considered a letter asking for medical food for children who are tube-fed to be provided under the gold card (universal health coverage).
it: Bilateral meetings abroad: cancelled or postponed for now
Contest videos (first round)
Model project for the quality of life of older persons, That Phanom District, Nakhon Phanom: passed to the subcommittee on older persons
Request to provide medical food for tube-fed children under the gold card

te: Reviewing laws after they take effect with King Prajadhipok's Institute, and a report on children and youth councils
se: The committee discussed the plan for the project on reviewing laws after they take effect with the College of Legislation, King Prajadhipok's Institute. It considered the contest videos, followed the plan to attend bilateral meetings on social affairs in the Netherlands and Belgium (31 Mar–8 Apr 2026), which will first be discussed with the Senate Affairs Committee, and resolved to present to the Senate the report of the subcommittee on children, “Proposals to Develop Structures and Multi-party Cooperation at the Local Community Level to Strengthen the Sustainability of Children and Youth Councils”.
it: Project on reviewing laws after they take effect (College of Legislation, King Prajadhipok's Institute invited)
Request to put the report on the sustainability of children and youth councils on the Senate agenda
Plan to attend bilateral meetings in the Netherlands and Belgium

te: Choosing contest videos, the volunteer role-model award, and results of following flood victims
se: The committee received a request from the ASEAN cultural promotion council to discuss the idea of a group marriage-equality event and passed it to the subcommittee on women. It chose videos in the individual category of the contest “Echoes of Hope for the Future of Thai Society”, followed the selection of “Senate Role Models Doing Good for the Nation: Volunteers Who Create Value and Inspire Society” from names sent in by the provinces, and considered the results of the field visit following help for vulnerable groups affected by floods.
it: Request to discuss a group marriage-equality event: passed to the subcommittee on women
Choosing videos in the individual category of the contest “Echoes of Hope for the Future of Thai Society”
Senate Role Models Doing Good for the Nation: volunteers who create value
Results of the field visit following help for vulnerable groups affected by floods

te: Funds and welfare for vulnerable groups: 4 ministries invited to give information
se: At the meeting on 10 Feb 2026 the committee noted the work of the subcommittees, such as the rights of people of diverse genders in military conscription and blood donation, laws to be adjusted after marriage equality, reproductive health of young people, and preparing the forum “Breaking Down the Walls that Block Education for Persons with Disabilities” (4 Mar 2026). It then discussed welfare and funds that help children, women, older persons, persons with disabilities and the disadvantaged with the Ministry of Social Development and Human Security, the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Labour and the Ministry of Public Health. It suggested reviewing how the funds are managed to keep up with the situation, telling people about their rights, adding ways to reach the funds, and linking the funds' databases so that help is not duplicated and no one is left out.
it: Work of all 3 subcommittees (children, youth and ethnic groups · older persons, persons with disabilities and the disadvantaged · women and people of diverse genders)
Field visit changed to Nakhon Phanom (19–20 Feb 2026)
Welfare and funds for vulnerable groups (Social Development and Human Security, Finance, Labour and Public Health invited)

te: Meeting 4/2569 · Committee on Social Development and Affairs of Children, Youth, Women, the Elderly, Persons with Disabilities, the Underprivileged and Social Diversity
Following help for flood victims in Songkhla, and results of the Phayao–Nan visit
se: The committee noted the schedule of a field visit to Songkhla (20 Jan 2026) to follow help, relief and recovery for vulnerable groups affected by floods in the South, with talks with the province and agencies and visits on physical and mental health care after the floods at Hat Yai Hospital and communities in Hat Yai City Municipality. It approved changes to the members of 2 subcommittees and noted the results of the visit to Phayao and Nan (14–17 Jan 2026), where it discussed the quality of life of vulnerable groups with the provinces and agencies.
it: Field visit to Songkhla: following help for vulnerable groups affected by floods
Changes to the members of the subcommittees on children and on older persons
Results of the field visit to Phayao and Nan (14–17 Jan 2026)

te: Cooperation on reviewing laws after they take effect, and the video contest “Echoes of Hope”
se: The committee considered progress on signing a cooperation agreement with King Prajadhipok's Institute on assessing laws after they take effect (Post Legislative Scrutiny), so that the committee can use this method to follow social laws. It noted progress of the video contest “Echoes of Hope for the Future of Thai Society”, whose deadline for entries was extended to 30 Jan 2026, on the topics of e-cigarettes, domestic violence, the power of older persons, and economic and social inequality.
it: Cooperation with King Prajadhipok's Institute on reviewing laws after they take effect (PLS)
Video contest “Echoes of Hope for the Future of Thai Society”: deadline for entries extended

te: Starting 2026: visits planned to Phayao, Nan, Songkhla and Nakhon Phanom, and a jobs-and-skills event at Parliament
se: At the first meeting of 2026 (7 Jan 2026) the committee planned field visits to follow the care of children, youth, women, older persons, persons with disabilities, the disadvantaged, people of diverse genders and ethnic groups in Phayao and Nan (14–17 Jan), Songkhla (20 Jan) and Sakon Nakhon–Nakhon Phanom (Feb). It prepared a forum and market fair, “Senate Joining Forces: Building Networks, Jobs and Livelihoods”, at Parliament (27–29 Jan) and cooperation with King Prajadhipok's Institute on reviewing laws after they take effect (Post Legislative Scrutiny). It also noted the work plans of the subcommittees, such as the proposal “Strong Women Provinces, Zero Domestic Violence”, a report on “The Power of Older Persons” and education for persons with disabilities.
it: Field visit plan to follow the care of vulnerable groups: Phayao, Nan, Songkhla, Sakon Nakhon and Nakhon Phanom
Forum and market fair “Senate Joining Forces: Building Networks, Jobs and Livelihoods”, and cooperation with King Prajadhipok's Institute on reviewing laws after they take effect
Work of all 3 subcommittees (children, youth and ethnic groups · older persons, persons with disabilities and the disadvantaged · women and people of diverse genders)

te: Low birth rate: the newborn child support grant and help for families
se: The meeting considered ways to respond to the low birth rate and to support healthy births and growth, with the Department of Children and Youth and the Department of Women's Affairs and Family Development. The Department of Children and Youth said the newborn child support grant is 600 baht a month; in fiscal year 2026 about 2 million children receive it, at more than 16,000 million baht. A universal scheme has been sent to the Secretariat of the Cabinet; if approved, about 5,600 million baht from the central budget would be sought in 2027. 96.43% of children aged 0–2 and 97.11% of children aged 3–6 are developing on track. The Department of Women's Affairs and Family Development said it is revising the domestic violence law and proposing leave to care for family members who fall suddenly ill.
it: Ways to respond to the low birth rate and to support healthy births and growth
The newborn child support grant of 600 baht a month, and the proposed universal scheme
Early-childhood development, and more than 50,000 child development centres that assessed themselves against the national standard
Revising the domestic violence law, leave to care for family, and support of up to 3,000 baht a year for low-income families

te: Meeting summary video · Low birth rate: the newborn child support grant and help for families
Low birth rate: local child development centres and childcare for workers' children
se: The meeting considered ways to respond to the low birth rate and to support healthy births and growth, with the Department of Local Administration and the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare. The Department of Local Administration said it is upgrading child development centres into local early-childhood and family centres, and is piloting care for children under 2 in 20 centres; 286 local authorities wish to take children under 2 and 111 already do. The Department of Labour Protection and Welfare said it has set up 2 model childcare centres in Nakhon Pathom and Samut Prakan for more than 870 workers' children, and extended the model to 16 private workplaces. The meeting proposed linking individual early-childhood data across ministries and using AI to help screen children at risk early.
it: Ways to respond to the low birth rate and to support healthy births and growth
Upgrading child development centres into local early-childhood and family centres, and taking children under 2
Model childcare centres for workers' children, 120 days of maternity leave, and flexible work under section 23/1
Proposals to link individual early-childhood data across ministries and to use AI to screen children at risk

te: Meeting summary video · Low birth rate: local child development centres and childcare for workers' children
Draft report on the ethnic groups law, and a study plan on the low birth rate
se: The meeting considered the draft study report on mechanisms to enforce the Act on the Protection and Promotion of the Ways of Life of Ethnic Groups B.E. 2025 and approved it in principle. The one-year study covers the setting up of the council for ethnic groups, with 211 members from 51 groups, and 3 pilot areas in Phang Nga, Lamphun and Uthai Thani. The key proposal is to speed up the declaration of protected areas for ethnic ways of life under section 37. The meeting asked for the draft to be revised before it goes to the committee, and planned a study visit to Chiang Rai, Phayao and Nan on 19–21 November 2026 to speed up the study on population structure and the low birth rate.
it: Draft study report on mechanisms to enforce the Act on the Protection and Promotion of the Ways of Life of Ethnic Groups B.E. 2025
Next work plan: study visit to Chiang Rai, Phayao and Nan, 19–21 November 2026
Finish both study reports by the end of November 2026 for the Senate

te: Meeting summary video · Draft report on the ethnic groups law, and a study plan on the low birth rate
Protecting children who face domestic violence, and how children are questioned in criminal cases
se: The meeting considered how to improve the handling of domestic violence against children under the Protection of Victims of Domestic Violence Act B.E. 2007, and the questioning of children by persons who perform this duty under the Criminal Procedure Code. The Social Work Professions Council, an association of psychologists and a social workers' club were invited. Participants said the training course for those who question children has been cut from 3 weeks to 9.5 days and has no government funding. Pay was raised from 500 to 1,000 baht a day, but it can be claimed only with 2 work orders in one day. Proposals included setting a minimum qualification of a bachelor's degree in psychology or social work, and using video-recorded interviews under section 172 ter so that children do not have to give statements again and again.
it: Domestic violence against children under the Protection of Victims of Domestic Violence Act B.E. 2007
Questioning of children under the Criminal Procedure Code: training, pay and duty rosters
Proposal for more guidance teachers (now 1 teacher for 400–500 children)
Proposals to revise the minimum qualifications in the ministerial regulation and to use section 172 ter instead of repeated child testimony
